A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HTTM study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching experiments relocated into the supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on 7Scenes, NRGBD, and ScanNet, inference timings, ablations, and token-similarity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds ETH3D reconstruction results in Table 1.

M1.justification: Head-wise merging, temporal reordering, query-only adaptive outlier filtering, and the first-frame anchoring variant are retained. Appendix C documents the existing procedure with pseudocode rather than establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds ETH3D reconstruction evaluation for weakly overlapped inputs. The existing 7Scenes, NRGBD, and ScanNet coverage remains, including the long-sequence experiments moved to Appendix B.1.

E2.justification: CUT3R, VGGT*, and FastVGGT retain their participation in the corresponding existing comparisons. The new ETH3D evaluation uses the already evaluated VGGT* and FastVGGT comparators; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Reported sampling strides, ScanNet scene selection, token ratios, and inference settings remain unchanged. ETH3D adds coverage without a separately specified protocol. Naming Chamfer distance in Table 1 clarifies the retained accuracy/completeness metrics.

E4.justification: The outlier-filtering ablation, spatial-versus-temporal merging analysis, and RoPE analyses are retained. The first-frame anchoring case study moves from Section 4.4 to Appendix B.2 with the same comparisons and findings.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-level variability. Existing averaging and quantile-based analyses are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds ETH3D accuracy/completeness values: VGGT* 0.087/0.053, FastVGGT 0.120/0.076, and HTTM 0.091/0.054. Previously reported reconstruction, latency, ablation, and trajectory results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and Appendix B's three propositions and proofs are retained. The new pseudocode supplies procedural documentation without adding or revising theoretical claims or derivations.

C1.justification: The training-free acceleration contribution and up-to-7× speedup claim remain unchanged. Adding 'over the original VGGT' in the abstract and conclusion makes an already established comparison explicit.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 replaces the assertion that shared merging produces repetitive token representations with the qualified explanation that it constrains head-specific aggregation and can reduce representational diversity. Other interpretations, including first-frame anchoring, are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix C provides pseudocode for accelerated global attention and outlier aggregation, explicitly documenting reordering, cluster assignments, filtering, centroid updates, and output restoration. Table 1 also identifies Chamfer distance; existing hardware and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Schöps et al. ETH3D benchmark reference. The remaining cited works and the paper's positioning relative to token-merging and VGGT acceleration methods are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. The long-sequence and error-mitigation sections move into Appendix B, Appendix C is added, and localized wording, author-contact information, and cross-references are revised.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains ETH3D columns. The long-sequence table moves into the supplement, and the trajectory figure is enlarged and rearranged from three columns to two, becoming Figure 13. Algorithm boxes and several caption refinements are added; existing visual findings are preserved.

improvement.justification: ETH3D adds reconstruction evidence for weakly overlapped inputs, and Appendix C improves implementation clarity through pseudocode. Existing experiments and proofs are preserved. These are useful, limited gains; sparse ETH3D evaluation details constrain the strength of the added evidence.
